title: Cheese and Tomato Lasagne
changes_from_base: Meat-free: a rich tomato sauce deepened with anchovy, layered with a pecorino cream sauce and fontina instead of ragù and béchamel.
summary: A meat-free lasagne with a deep tomato sauce, a pecorino cream sauce and fontina, browned on top.

steps.title: Cheese sauce
steps.text: Whisk the 90 g pecorino, cottage cheese, cream, garlic, cornflour and pepper until smooth.

steps.title: Tomato sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil in the saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion with the sugar, chilli and oregano for 10 min until soft. Add the garlic and anchovies for 2 min; they melt away and give a savoury depth without tasting of fish. Stir in both tins of tomatoes, the purée and the 20 g pecorino, and simmer about 20 min until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Soak the sheets
steps.text: Meanwhile cover the sheets with boiling water in the baking dish and leave 15 min until pliable, separating them with a knife tip. Drain, rinse with cold water, pat dry and dry the dish. Cut 2 sheets in half. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan).

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread about 360 ml tomato sauce in the dish and make a layer of 3½ sheets, then half the cheese sauce and 60 g fontina. Add a second layer of sheets, 360 ml tomato sauce and 60 g fontina, then a third layer with the rest of the cheese sauce and 60 g fontina. Finish with the last sheets and the remaining tomato sauce, fontina and pecorino.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover with oiled foil and bake 35 min. Uncover, raise the oven to 250 °C (230 °C fan) and bake 10-15 min until lightly browned. Rest 20 min and scatter with basil before cutting.

tips: Mince the anchovies finely so they melt into the sauce.
Alternate the half sheets to keep the lasagne level.
Watch the final high-heat browning closely.
storage: Cool, cover and refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat covered in a 180 °C oven until piping hot (74 °C) in the centre.
